headline: Bank of America strategists say they are staying cautious on stocks for the next three to four weeks because of higher real interest rates, geopolitical risks and shaky AI-linked shares.
score_reason: Widely followed strategist note, but an opinion rather than an event and it was written on 15 Oct.
importance_line: Investors in shares and AI-linked funds are affected first, and borrowers who pay market interest rates would feel a Fed hike, though BofA's call for an October hike is more hawkish than market pricing, according to Bloomberg.
summary: Investing.com reports that Bank of America strategists led by Michael Hartnett "continue to lean risk-off" (favouring safer assets) for the next three to four weeks, citing 3% real yields (the return on bonds after inflation), geopolitical risks, US midterm election uncertainty and weak price action in AI-linked stocks. They expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates on 28 Oct and say AI spenders and lenders are under pressure, with private equity funds and business development companies, which lend to private firms, back at their 2026 lows and the cost of insuring Oracle's debt a stress point.
notes: The Investing.com article was read on its Yahoo Finance copy (investing.com page 403); Bloomberg's report on the same BofA note, also read on Yahoo, dates the note 15 Oct and calls its October-hike view more hawkish than market pricing.
